body_markdown:
When it comes to motorcycles, Billy Joel is not *An Innocent Man.* *Don’t Ask Me Why* , but over the years he has amassed a huge collection of bikes, and more than 70 of them will be for sale during[Retromobile New York](https://www.goodingco.com/auction/retromobile-new-york-auctions-2026) in November.


The Billy Joel Motorcycle Collection will be on show at Christie’s Rockefeller Center from October 8-12 before going under the hammer at the Gooding Christie’s Javits Center auction on November 20-21.


Joel, now 77 years old, has sold more than 150 million records in his five-decade career, and won six Grammy awards. You’ll find his name in the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, the Songwriters Hall of Fame, and the Hollywood Walk of Fame, but he definitely preferred to ride.


Dan Weaks / Billy Joel Archives


Joel picked and chose his collection carefully and kept his bikes at his[20th Century Cycles](https://20thcenturycycles.com/) shop in Oyster Bay, New York, where each one was carefully maintained, and many were updated to make them more rideable. One notable machine, however, was a gift. Having sold out 150 shows at Madison Square Garden, the venue presented Joel with a unique[1978 Triumph T140 Bonneville](https://www.goodingco.com/lot/1978-triumph-t140-bonneville) , with custom paintwork and an accompanying helmet listing the date of every one of his shows.


Over the years, Joel collected BMWs, Moto Guzzis, Harley-Davidsons, Yamahas, Triumphs, Hondas, and Kawasakis. He was a *Ducatisti* , as exemplified by the[1982 900 Mike Hailwood Replica](https://www.goodingco.com/lot/1982-ducati-900-mike-hailwood-replica) and the[1975 Supersport](https://www.goodingco.com/lot/1975-ducati-750-sport-rn26) in the auction. The former was released by Ducati to mark Hailwood’s 1978 incredible victory in the Isle of Man TT, on his return after hanging up his helmet 11 years prior. The Supersport, meanwhile, was arguably *the* superbike of the Seventies, combining near-legendary high-speed handling with race-bred Italian styling.


“I’ve always been drawn to bikes built by people who cared about getting every detail right,” says Joel. “I’ve loved building this collection. Now it’s someone else’s turn to hit the road.”


Joel’s motorcycles are being sold with no reserve, so you don’t need to be a *Big Shot* to buy one, and all proceeds from the sale will go to The Joel Foundation, which supports motherless babies, widows in the community, and rural healthcare centers.


If you know an *Uptown Girl* who loves bikes, then *Tell Her About It.*
